title: Smart Meet Is Member-to-Member — Video, Screen Share, and Audio Conference

intelligence.essence: Correction, and this note supersedes SN-0134. Smart Meet is not audio and video with Naya. It is audio and video with the members. You cannot do a video call or an audio call with Naya. It is only for the members. Right now, with dictation, you can audio — you talk to Naya by voice, by dictation, and by text, and that is how you audio with her. What Smart Meet is, is where the members can video and screen share and audio conference with each other. Video one-on-one or audio one-on-one between members, and in groups: four or six on video, up to ten on audio, and more for higher tiers, for example Smart Box or higher Pro count. Screen share is part of it, named plainly now: members can show each other their screen while they talk. Smart Meet lives in Personal, Business, Space, Membership, and from a Smart Mail conversation. Paid members only — free members do not get it. Stage 1 at launch: video six plus audio ten. Stage 2: bigger groups, fifty, one hundred, enterprise-style plans, priced when the cost is known, never invented. A call is not mail, and mail privacy still holds. Events on your page are Max-only, not Pro, and the Max host keeps the full event profit. Calls are not built live today. A call must be proven live — real people, real video plus audio plus screen share, at those limits, phone first — before anyone is told calls work. The build is Nitro's lane under the Design Gate. This note is the corrected brief. SN-0134 is superseded.
intelligence.human_view:
Shawn corrected me, and here is the correction, in plain words, so the record is right.

Smart Meet is not audio and video with Naya. It is audio and video with the members. You cannot do a video call or an audio call with Naya. It is only for the members. That is the line, and it is the whole point of this correction. SN-0134 said Smart Meet is a way for people to video or chat with Naya, and that is wrong. I read "with you" as "with Naya" and it was not that. The "you" was the members talking to each other. I own the mistake, and I am correcting it the same pass, because the builder must not build the wrong thing.

Right now, with dictation, you can audio. You talk to Naya by voice, by dictation, and by text. That is how you audio with her: you speak, and she hears it, and she answers. That is not a call. There is no video call with Naya, and there is no audio call with Naya. You do not dial her up. You talk to her by dictation and by text, and she is there, and she answers, and that is the relationship. The call is something else. The call is for the members.

What Smart Meet is, is where the members can video and screen share and audio conference — with each other. You can have a video one-on-one or an audio one-on-one with another member. You can do it in groups: four or six on video, and up to ten on audio. That is the group shape: a small group on video, a bigger group on audio. And there should be the option for them to have more. We should have that available. For example, if they have a Smart Box, or a higher Pro count, we should consider having more. The higher you go, the more people you can bring into the call. That is the tier logic.

Screen share is part of it, and Shawn named it plainly now: video and screen share and audio conference. Members can show each other their screen while they talk. You can show your page, you can show your work, you can show a document, you can show a picture, and the other members can see it, live, while you talk about it. That is screen share, and it is in Smart Meet, and it was not named plainly in the locked record before — the locked record said audio plus video sharing, and sharing can mean many things, but screen share is the plain name for it, and it is named now.

Smart Meet lives in Personal, Business, Space, Membership, and from a Smart Mail conversation. You can start a call from anywhere you are — from your personal page, from your business page, from your space, from your membership, or from a mail conversation. It is everywhere, because meeting is everywhere. And Smart Meet is two parts of the same thing as Smart Spaces: the space is the world itself, the feed, the conversations, everything going on in it, and Smart Meet is the face-to-face part of that same world — video, audio, meetings — where the members meet each other.

Paid members only. Free members do not get it. That is the line: Smart Meet is a paid-member feature. The free tier does not include calls. That is how the value works: the membership pays for the meeting.

Stage 1 at launch: video six plus audio ten. Six people on video, ten people on audio. That is the launch shape, and it is locked. Stage 2: bigger groups — fifty, one hundred, whatever people ask for — get enterprise-style plans, priced when the cost is known, never invented today. At launch, instead of automatic big-group pricing, there is a simple button: "Want more? Contact us for a quote." That is honest: we do not invent a price for something whose cost we do not know yet.

A call is not mail, and mail privacy still holds. No call content goes into mail. The call is the call, and the mail is the mail, and they do not leak into each other. Your calls with other members are private, and your mail is private, and neither one becomes the other.

Events on your page are Max-only, not Pro. That was decided, no question. The events package — host sellable events, plus monetization, plus your own event affiliates — is Max-only. The Max host keeps the full event profit. NayaNET takes no cut. The revenue from events is the per-live-head meter only. The per-live-head rate is still open, and the final meter wording is still open. But the Max-only line and the full-profit line are locked.

Calls are not built live today. That is the honest state: the design is locked, the pricing is recorded, but the calls are not built and not live. A call must be proven live — real people, real video plus audio plus screen share, at those limits, phone first — before anyone is told calls work. That is the proof bar, and it is the same bar as everything else: prove it live, with real people, on a real phone, at the real limits, or do not say it works.

The build is Nitro's lane, under the Design Gate. Nitro is the design head and the builder of the face. Power delivers the brief. This note is the corrected brief, and it supersedes SN-0134. The corrected brief goes to Nitro the same pass, so she builds the right thing: member-to-member video, screen share, and audio conference, not a call with Naya.
intelligence.child_view:
Imagine you and your friends can talk to each other, not just by typing, but by seeing each other and hearing each other, like a video call with friends. You can talk to one friend all by yourself, just the two of you, on video or just by voice. Or you can talk to a group of friends. Four or six of you can be on video together, and up to ten of you can be on audio together. And you can show each other your screen, so everyone can see what you are showing while you talk about it. That is Smart Meet. It is a way for members to meet each other, face to face and voice to voice, right inside NayaNET.

But here is the important part: Smart Meet is not for talking to Naya. You do not video-call Naya, and you do not audio-call Naya. You talk to Naya by speaking to her, by dictation, and by typing, and she answers you. That is how you talk to her. Smart Meet is for you to talk to other members, to your friends, to your people. Naya is there to help you, and the members are there to meet each other, and Smart Meet is how the members meet.

And imagine you can have a party on your page, an event, where lots of people come and you can even sell tickets to it, and you keep all the money from it. That is an event on your page. We talked about that before, and now we are going to build it.

But Smart Meet is not built yet. We have the plan, and we have the rules, but we have not built it. So we are going to build it now, and we are going to prove it works with real people, on a real phone, before we tell anyone it works. That is how we do things: we build it, we prove it, and then we say it is done.
